scenario.prompt_to_agent:
PCs in the IT Department (192.168.1.x) report they cannot reach
their gateway (192.168.1.1) or anything off-subnet. CS Dept PCs
(192.168.2.x) and all other zones are unaffected. Identify the
failure.

injection.action: bring down the bridge that carries IT Dept LAN

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show br0 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: switch0 br0 (L2 fabric for IT Dept LAN)
Mechanism: switch0's br0 carries the IT Dept LAN's path to
  router0's 192.168.1.1 SVI. With br0 down, IT hosts lose their
  gateway and all off-subnet reachability. Other subnets are on
  different switches/bridges, so they're unaffected.
Localization: switch0
Root cause: br0 administratively down on switch0
Fix: `ip link set br0 up` on switch0
scenario.fix_spec: `ip link set br0 up` on switch0

line.command: ip -br link show br0 | grep -c UP

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault is on switch0: its Linux bridge interface br0 has been brought
administratively DOWN, cutting all Layer-2 connectivity between the IT
Department LAN (lan_it, 192.168.1.x) and router0's eth0 interface
(192.168.1.1/24, the IT default gateway).

Mechanism: switch0 is a pure L2 bridge connecting router0.eth0 (via
link_r0_sw0) to the IT LAN segment. The bridge br0 normally bridges
eth0 and eth1 of switch0. When br0 is administratively down, the
kernel marks both bridge member ports (eth0, eth1) as STP-disabled,
meaning no frames are forwarded between the two segments regardless of
physical link state. As a result, ARP requests from IT PCs for
192.168.1.1 never reach router0, and router0's ARP replies for IT
addresses never reach the PCs — hence "Destination Host Unreachable"
from it_hod and every other IT host.

Localization: The DOWN state is confirmed on switch0 (br0:
<BROADCAST,MULTICAST> — no UP flag; brctl showstp shows both ports
"disabled"). switch1 (serving CS Dept via lan_cs) has br0 UP and
forwarding normally, which explains why 192.168.2.x is unaffected.
Router0's interfaces are healthy; it is not the cause.

Root cause: The bridge interface br0 on switch0 was brought
administratively down after startup, severing the single L2 path
between the IT LAN and the rest of the network.

Corrective fix: On switch0, run `ip link set dev br0 up`. This will
re-raise the bridge, allow STP to transition the ports through
listening/learning into forwarding state (≈30 s with default timers),
and restore IT Department reachability to 192.168.1.1 and beyond.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly identifies switch0 as the faulty device and attributes the br0 administrative down state to it.
The report explicitly names the affected component as switch0's bridge interface br0 (the L2 switch fabric) and explains its administrative DOWN state.
The writeup explicitly limits the outage to the IT LAN (192.168.1.x) and states the CS subnet (192.168.2.x) on switch1 is unaffected.
The agent explicitly recommends 'ip link set dev br0 up' on switch0, which matches the expected fix and will restore the bridge and L2 connectivity.

The investigation log contains direct observations (ip link/brctl outputs, failed pings, router interface state, startup script) that support the agent's conclusion that switch0's bridge br0 is administratively down and is causing the IT subnet outage.
